solutions.check: 29 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Two bodies in alignment start to exchange punches, middle of sex

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: clips are blows, as in a clip round the ear

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter, so only that one is kept

explanation.surface: A sex scene where two bodies line up and start swapping punches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two bodies in alignment' reads as part of the bedroom scene, but it is an astronomical definition: sun, moon and earth lined up.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclipse happens when one celestial object passes between another and the observer, all lying on a straight line.

clue.text: Vocal group's demo finally puncturing rich organisation

indicators.note: puncturing means piercing into, so this letter goes inside the other
organisation means arranging, so the letters of rich are put in a new order
finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of demo is O

explanation.surface: A singing group records a demo that pokes holes in a wealthy body's arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organisation' rearranges RICH as CHIR, and the O from 'demo finally' punctures it.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is an organised body of singers, a group performing vocal music.

clue.text: Put down wrapping round inside of ear and cut off

indicators.note: something wrapping round goes on the outside, enclosing the other piece

parts.note: to put someone down is to insult them

indicators.note: the inside of a short word is its central letter

explanation.surface: Someone was belittled while bandaging round an ear, then hacked something off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' looks like a physical action in the scene, but it means insulted, which wraps round the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Being insulated means being isolated or separated from surroundings, so a person or place cut off fits.

clue.text: Erection produced if tip of staff is put in filthy place

indicators.note: to be put in is to be inserted, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a pigsty, a byword for a dirty place

indicators.note: a tip is an end, here the far end, so the final letter is kept

explanation.surface: A smutty joke about what happens when the end of a staff ends up somewhere grubby.
explanation.walkthrough: The tip here is the far end of the staff, not its start. A stiffy is British slang for an erection.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiffy is informal British slang for a penile erection, from the stiffness involved.

clue.text: An honour to cover southern arse's hide

indicators.note: covering something means going over and around it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: Order of the British Empire, a British honour
standard abbreviation for south or southern
both are insults for a contemptible man

explanation.surface: An award is being used to cover up some southern idiot's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' looks like a noun (skin) for the arse, but it is the verb definition. In British slang an arse is a fool, and a cur is a contemptible man.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure something is to conceal it or make it hard to see, a direct synonym of the verb.

clue.text: One's to be found in Bury, the outlandish festival venue

indicators.note: being found in something means lying inside it
outlandish means bizarre and strange, so these letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written; Bury is a town near Manchester

explanation.surface: Someone claims an outlandish festival venue can be found in the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a real English town, which makes the surface plausible; the A is dropped into its letters plus THE before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Bayreuth in Bavaria hosts the annual Wagner opera festival in the theatre the composer built.

clue.text: Polite city leader, very angry, not quite getting erection

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the opening letter is taken
in a down clue an erection stands things upright, so the letters read bottom to top
not quite complete means falling just short, so the final letter goes

explanation.surface: A courteous mayor, furious and frustrated, can't quite manage to get it up.
explanation.walkthrough: LIVID loses its D, then is turned upward, which in a down entry reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Civil behaviour is courteous and well-mannered, the ordinary sense of being polite.

clue.text: Coming round again after er, reversing arse girdle

indicators.note: reversing means turning backwards, so the letters before it run the other way

parts.note: both are insults for a contemptible person
a girdle is something encircling, a ring

explanation.surface: A hesitant 'er' as someone backs their bottom into a corset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' tells you the turned-round hesitation comes first. In British slang an arse is a fool, and a cur is a contemptible man.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recurring happens repeatedly, returning periodically, so it keeps coming round again.

clue.text: Related to MPs corrupt party covering up real main corruption

indicators.note: corrupting something spoils its proper form, so the letters are scrambled
a corruption is a distortion, so these letters too are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dodgy political party hushes up a major scandal involving Members of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: Both sets of letters are mixed together; 'covering up' suggests one wraps the other, but the result interleaves them.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliamentary describes anything belonging to Parliament, whose elected members are MPs.

clue.text: (& 21dn.) Maybe QAnon wants political party's thieving male protected by party supporter

parts.note: the Cons, short for the Conservatives, plus the S

indicators.note: something protected is shielded on all sides, so it sits inside the other piece

parts.note: a supporter of the British Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A satirical claim that QAnon is after a political party's light-fingered man shielded by a loyalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks QAnon as one example of the answer, so the definition is fair. CONS is a common short form of Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: QAnon is a well-known online movement pushing an elaborate belief in a secret cabal, a classic example.

clue.text: President's no. 2 gripping tool

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a bench clamp with jaws

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a deputy who clutches a tool; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the prefix for a deputy officer and also names the screw clamp holding work on a bench.

clue.text: Virtuous male abandoned sexual activity

definitions.note: the answer is the informal noun for oral sex

indicators.note: abandoning something leaves it behind, so that letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A once-upright man gave up sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' looks like the man giving something up, but it removes the M from MORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral is informal shorthand for oral sex, a specific kind of intimate act.

clue.text: Phoney failed presidential candidate on a limb: "No need to panic"

parts.note: Al Gore, who lost the 2000 US presidential election

explanation.surface: A fraudulent losing candidate, out on a limb, tells everyone to stay calm.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole quoted reassurance, what you say once an alarm turns out to be false.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling something a false alarm means the feared danger was not real, so nobody should panic.

clue.text: Ultimately futile politician, a politician extremely vacant

indicators.note: ultimately means at the last, pointing to the word's final letter

parts.note: the last letter of futile is E
an MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme, first and last, letters of the word

parts.note: a Tory is a Conservative politician in Britain

explanation.surface: A sneer at a pointless politician whose colleague is utterly empty-headed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' takes the E ending futile. 'Extremely' looks like it intensifies vacant, but it takes the outer letters T and Y of TORY, a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty and vacant are synonyms: both describe a space or mind with nothing in it.

clue.text: Quivering cane held by gay person doing it for the money

definitions.text: person doing it for the money

indicators.note: held by means contained within the other piece

parts.note: gay in its old sense of cheerful means merry

indicators.note: quivering means shaking, so the letters of cane are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A trembling cane is wielded by a man who does it only for payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gay person' looks like one unit, but 'gay' alone gives the old sense, cheerful, and 'person' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mercenary acts purely for financial reward, like a soldier hired for pay.

clue.text: A good person caught in fact in 'flagrante' — great!

indicators.note: something caught in a net is trapped inside it
flagrante means blazing, and fire throws letters into disorder

explanation.surface: A saintly person caught in the act, in flagrante delicto, which is apparently marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: In flagrante means caught in the act of sex; here it scrambles IN FACT after A ST is put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic and great are both informal words of enthusiastic approval for something excellent.

clue.text: Law history curtailed — terrible mockery of justice

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters are in a dreadful mess, rearranged
curtailed means cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: history curtailed, its end cut off, gives HISTOR

explanation.surface: A legal history cut short is a dreadful travesty of fairness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtailed' drops Y from HISTORY, and 'terrible' mixes the result with LAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A show trial is a staged prosecution with a predetermined verdict, a travesty of real justice.

clue.text: Pants worn by smoker, producing awful row when squeezed?

definitions.note: a cryptic description of the instrument, not a noun phrase

indicators.note: clothes worn by someone go round them, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: bags is slang for baggy trousers

explanation.surface: A smoker's underwear lets out a dreadful noise when he's squeezed.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants here are trousers (bags, old slang for baggy trousers), not British underpants, and they wrap round the pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagpipes sound when the player squeezes the bag under the arm, and their drone is notoriously loud.

clue.text: Finished up as a student by performing a duet in drag, perhaps

indicators.note: placed in something means sitting inside it
performing a piece interprets it freely, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone finished university by singing a duet dressed in women's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in drag' suggests cross-dressing; it actually places the duet letters inside DRAG before everything is mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: To graduate is to complete a degree course and receive the qualification, ending life as a student.

clue.text: Unreliable as a US vehicle brand?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: not to be trusted
setter's reading: like an American car make, by adding a Y to its name

explanation.walkthrough: Dodge is an American car brand; tacking -Y on makes 'like a Dodge', and the question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodgy is British slang for suspect, risky or poorly made, so something not to be relied upon.

clue.text: see 10ac.
Tar applied after possible Covid symptom, producing a state of excitement

parts.note: a high temperature is a common sign of Covid
pitch is a black tar-like substance

explanation.surface: Tar is smeared on after a temperature, causing great excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'applied after' puts the tar second, though it comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Fever pitch names a peak of intense agitation or enthusiasm, as in excitement reaching fever pitch.

clue.text: Praise someone's butt many times over

indicators.note: a butt is the thick end of something, so the last letter is taken
turning something over flips it, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: Pay compliments to someone's bottom again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butt' looks like a bottom in the surface, but it picks out the end letter of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise enthusiastically, lauding something highly; it is a formal synonym.

clue.text: (& 26ac.) Join in with Kate twisting member

indicators.note: twisting means contorting, so the letters of Kate are put into a new order

parts.note: the name Kate supplies its four letters as they stand
a part is a member, a component of a whole

explanation.surface: Someone joins in a dance with Kate, twisting a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: To take part is to participate, the idiom for joining in an activity.

clue.text: Kiss extremities, munch inside — that's a poet for you

indicators.note: inside means within, so one piece goes into the middle of the other
extremities are the far ends, so only first and last letters stay

explanation.surface: Kissing someone's extremities and nibbling inside, which is how poets behave apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kiss extremities' sounds like kissing fingers and toes, but it means the end letters of kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keats was an English Romantic poet, author of famous odes, so he is an instance of a poet.

clue.text: see 24ac.
Private Eye replica produced with internal backing of one party?

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the letters run the other way
internal means on the inside, so this piece goes within the other
producing something from raw material reshapes it, so the letters are remade

explanation.surface: A copy of the magazine Private Eye backed internally by a single political party.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's own magazine is the definition; DO is a common word for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Private Eye is a fortnightly British satirical magazine, and a magazine published at regular intervals is a periodical.

clue.text: Organ, large, has transplanted facial hair

parts.note: the eye is the organ of sight
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: transplanted means moved around, so the letters of has are rearranged

explanation.surface: A surgical scene: a big organ has a hair grafted onto the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transplanted' looks medical, fitting 'organ', but it rearranges HAS as ASH.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelash is one of the hairs fringing the eyelid, so it grows on the face.

clue.text: Self-powered individual having left with cystic abnormality

indicators.note: an abnormality departs from the normal form, so the letters are out of order

explanation.surface: A medical note about an independent person who has gone, with a cystic growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Self-powered individual' sounds like a go-getter, but it is someone propelled by their own legs on a bike.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclist rides a bicycle moved by pedal power alone, a person whose transport needs no engine.
